description: We are currently a team of three composed of Taiwanese people. We are fascinated by manor simulation games. We also have interest/expertise in GIS to some extent.
summary: Mission Mars is a browser-based simulation game for ages 7–12 that turns kids into junior astronaut trainees. Players run a Mars mission for 30 sols (Martian days). They split limited power between life support and science, shelter from solar storms, and fixing breakdowns, so every decision is critical. The game addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by letting children experience space weather and radiation risks hands-on instead of just reading about them, aiming to build planning skills, science literacy, and curiosity about space exploration through play.
details:
Mission Mars puts kids in charge of a simulated Mars mission. Each sol, they choose how to spend limited power: whether to hide in the shelter from a solar storm, whether to risk a spacewalk to clean the solar panels, and whether to fix a system breakdown with the crew or ask Earth, and the radio delay costs time. Every choice has a gain and a cost, and a short summary at the end shows what the crew went through. There are three difficulty levels, from Cadet (friendly for kids) to Commander (for older siblings or parents) and Superstorm, and the game is playable in English and two other languages.

Kids learn to plan, prioritize, and accept trade-offs, and they get a feel for space weather and radiation risk without needing to know the actual scientific theory.

The game is plain JavaScript with three.js for the nice-looking 3D island scene. The backend is Python (FastAPI).

The look is friendly rather than technical. For enjoyment, the game has an opening cinematic, a guided training mission, postcard functions, and a crew diary.
